learning_objective: 🧠 Map the biological supercomputer—the human brain and nervous system—and learn how electrical signals travel in milliseconds!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Divided into two parts: The Central Neural System (CNS) includes the brain and spinal cord, acting as the main control center. The Peripheral Neural System (PNS) comprises all the nerves extending from the CNS to the rest of the body.
A neuron has three main parts: Dendrites (branch-like extensions that receive signals), a Cell body (soma), and an Axon (a long tail that transmits the electrical signal away from the cell body).

Neurons are naturally polarized (negative inside, positive outside) due to the Na+/K+ pump. When stimulated, Sodium channels open, Na+ rushes in, and the inside becomes positive (Depolarization). This electrical wave travels down the axon.

Neurons don't actually touch. The gap between them is a synapse. When an electrical signal reaches the end of an axon, it bursts open tiny sacs (vesicles) releasing chemicals called Neurotransmitters. These chemicals cross the gap to trigger the next neuron.

Forebrain: Cerebrum (memory, logic) and Hypothalamus (temperature, hunger). Midbrain: visual/auditory reflexes. Hindbrain: Cerebellum (balance and coordination) and Medulla (controls involuntary vital functions like breathing and heart rate).

fun_activity.title: 🔥 The Knee-Jerk Reflex
fun_activity.instructions: Sit on a chair with your legs dangling freely. Have someone gently but firmly tap the tendon just below your kneecap with the edge of their hand. Your leg will kick up instantly on its own! This is a reflex arc happening entirely through your spinal cord, completely bypassing the brain to save time.

exam_tips: 📌 The Resting Membrane Potential is maintained by the Sodium-Potassium pump, which actively transports 3 Na+ outwards for every 2 K+ into the cell, costing ATP.
📌 Myelin sheath (secreted by Schwann cells) acts as an insulator around the axon, allowing electrical signals to jump rapidly from node to node (Nodes of Ranvier) in saltatory conduction.
📌 The Limbic system (along with the hypothalamus) is responsible for regulating sexual behavior, emotional reactions (excitement, fear, pleasure), and motivation.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Corpus Callosum is a tract of nerve fibers that connects the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
⭐ Unipolar neurons (cell body with one axon only) are usually found in the embryonic stage.
⭐ Acetylcholine is the most common excitatory neurotransmitter at chemical synapses.
